standard.title: Method for Spectrophotometric Determination of Nitrite (स्पेक्ट्रम प्रकाशमिति द्वारा नाइट्राइट ज्ञात करने की पद्धति)
standard.description: This standard prescribes three distinct analytical methods for the quantitative determination of nitrite in chemical and technical samples using spectrophotometric and ultraviolet (UV) absorption techniques.
standard.scope: This standard prescribes three distinct analytical methods for the quantitative determination of nitrite in chemical and technical samples using spectrophotometric and ultraviolet (UV) absorption techniques.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 13565 : 1992 is a laboratory testing methodology rather than a direct physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its sampling, container extraction, and spectrophotometric calculation protocols is strictly required in public sector chemical quality audits, industrial corrosion-preventive testing, and environmental monitoring across India to certify nitrite concentrations.
requirements: Prescribes a spectrophotometric method for nitrite determination using the diazotisation and coupling reaction of sulphanilic acid and 1-naphthylamine, forming a highly colored red azo dye measured in the visible spectrum.
Prescribes a UV spectrophotometry method using sulphanilic acid to measure the absorbance of the diazotised complex in the ultraviolet spectrum.
Prescribes a UV differential spectrophotometry method using sulphamic acid, measuring absorbance differences to isolate and calculate nitrite concentrations.
Before drawing sample aliquots from opaque glass containers, the technician must carefully remove the cap or lid so that a mechanical stirrer may be inserted directly without disturbing sediment.

For metal containers having a removable cap or lid, open by removing it. If no removable closure is provided, the operator must open the container by punching two holes on opposite sides of the top of the container, subsequent to which one of these openings must be enlarged with metal shears to provide adequate room for stirring and pipetting.

To ensure a perfectly homogeneous mixture prior to analysis, the sample must be mixed thoroughly for exactly 5 minutes using a stirring device capable of agitating the material sufficiently to suspend all separated solids and disperse any supernatant phases (liquid or solid) without drawing air into the mixture.

Because technical samples containing nitrite (like corrosion preventives or antifreeze) may contain flammable solvents, the stirring device must be safe to use with inflammable liquids, such as methanol. A sparkless, brushless type induction motor or an air-driven motor of sufficient capacity are suggested. The stirrer design must fit into the smallest container opening.

In reporting the results of any test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it must be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified limit in the standard.
